headline: A Simple Diet May Slow Brain Aging by 2.5 Years
meta_description: New research shows the MIND diet slows brain shrinkage and grey matter loss, with effects equivalent to delaying aging by 2.5 years.
summary_short: Following the MIND diet more closely slows brain tissue loss and delays structural signs of aging, according to a major 20-year study.
body:
A long-term study of over 1,600 middle-aged and older adults has found that eating according to the MIND diet—a combination of Mediterranean and heart-healthy principles—may slow the brain changes that occur with aging. Research published in the Journal of Neurology Neurosurgery & Psychiatry shows that people who followed the diet more closely experienced slower loss of grey matter, the brain tissue crucial for memory, learning, and decision-making. The effect was striking: every three-point increase in diet adherence corresponded to a 20 percent reduction in age-related decline, equivalent to roughly 2.5 years of delayed brain aging.

The MIND diet emphasizes leafy greens, berries, nuts, whole grains, fish, beans, poultry, and olive oil while limiting butter, red meat, sweets, and fried foods. Researchers tracked 1,647 participants from the Framingham Heart Study Offspring cohort between 1999 and 2019, collecting regular brain MRI scans every two to six years. Berries and poultry emerged as particularly protective foods, while sweets and fried fast foods showed the opposite effect, linked to faster brain tissue loss. The benefits appeared stronger in older adults, suggesting the diet may be especially valuable for those at higher risk of cognitive decline.

What makes this finding encouraging is not just the diet's simplicity, but its accessibility. Participants needed only moderate adherence—the average score was under 7 out of a possible 15—to see measurable benefits. The researchers note that combining the MIND diet with physical activity and maintaining a healthy weight amplified the protective effects, pointing toward a realistic path for maintaining brain health as we age.
quick_facts: 1,647 middle-aged and older adults followed for average 12 years
MIND diet slows grey matter loss by 20 percent per 3-point score increase
Berries and poultry linked to healthier brain structure; sweets and fried foods to greater loss
Effects equivalent to delaying brain aging by approximately 2.5 years
Benefits stronger in older adults and those who exercise regularly
